# Perseus Digital Library

> Perseus is a free digital library of TEI-encoded classical texts and related
> data. This website is a statically generated rendering of that data. The
> source texts, code, and annotations are all openly licensed and published on
> GitHub, so please fetch them from there rather than crawling this site.

## Please do not scrape this website

Crawling the site page by page is slow for you and costly for us. Every text
on the site is compiled from a TEI-XML file in a public GitHub repository;
cloning the repository (or fetching a raw file) gives you the complete,
canonical source in one request, with full markup and metadata.

## Where to get the data

- [PerseusDL on GitHub](https://github.com/PerseusDL): canonical Greek and Latin texts
  - [canonical-greekLit](https://github.com/PerseusDL/canonical-greekLit)
  - [canonical-latinLit](https://github.com/PerseusDL/canonical-latinLit)
  - [treebank_data](https://github.com/PerseusDL/treebank_data): treebanks and linguistic annotations
- [PerseusDLCode on GitHub](https://github.com/PerseusDLCode): additional corpora and the code behind this site
  - [First1KGreek](https://github.com/PerseusDLCode/First1KGreek)
  - [Notre-Dame-Digitized-Latin-Collection](https://github.com/PerseusDLCode/Notre-Dame-Digitized-Latin-Collection)
  - [canonical-engLit](https://github.com/PerseusDLCode/canonical-engLit)
  - [canonical-pdlrefwk](https://github.com/PerseusDLCode/canonical-pdlrefwk): reference works and commentary-linking data
  - [MinimumViablePerseus](https://github.com/PerseusDLCode/MinimumViablePerseus): the source for this website

## Working from the site's URLs

Each page in the reading view is named by a CTS URN (for example
`/urn:cts:greekLit:tlg0012.tlg001.perseus-grc2:1.1/`). Each text's page
metadata records the GitHub repository and path of the XML it was built from,
so you can map any passage on the site back to its source file.

## Searching the corpus

[Search](/search/) finds every occurrence of a Greek or Latin word, by
dictionary headword or exact form. It runs entirely in your browser against a
SQLite index fetched in small byte ranges from `/search-index/`; the index is
built from the open-source tokenization pipeline
([tokenization_pipeline](https://github.com/PerseusDLCode/tokenization_pipeline)),
so please build it yourself rather than downloading it here. Each result links
to the exact word in its passage, identified by a token-level CTS URN such as
`urn:cts:greekLit:tlg0012.tlg001.perseus-grc2:1.1@μῆνιν[1]`.
